one_month_reasoning: Three scheduled events fall in the window: September revenue on Oct 8 at 13:30 Taipei (TSMC financial calendar; I had Oct 9-10 in round 1), Q3 2026 results and Q4 guidance on Oct 15, and the FOMC on Oct 27-28. July+August revenue (NT$982B) means even a September at or below August beats the $44.6-45.8B guide, and consensus Q3 ADR EPS of $4.46 already sits above the guide midpoint, so the beat is expected. The swing factors are Q4 gross-margin guidance (N2 dilution) and any 2027 capex framing; the sell side is at $75-90B, so a number at the high end could be read as either demand confirmation or FCF pressure. The 10-year touched its highest level since 2002 on Oct 1 (~5.24-5.29%) with the Fed hiking, which offsets the small post-beat drift TSMC usually gets. I set the median at ~$461.5 (+0.5%) and widen sigma slightly to ~12% (monthly vol 11.4% x1.05) for earnings plus FOMC.

fair_value.method: Blend of 19.5x Oct-2027 NTM EPS ($24.9 -> $486, weight 0.7) and a 5-year FCF DCF with $85B 2027 capex, 10.0% cost of equity on a 5.25% risk-free rate and 4% terminal growth ($353, weight 0.3) = ~$446 per ADR.

inputs_detail.value: $21.93 (13 analysts; up from $19.66 90 days ago, 9 up / 0 down in 30 days)

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2027 consensus x1.18. Management says capex over the next three years will be 'significantly higher' and AI demand runs strong to 2029-30; UBS models 2027 revenue +40% and 2028 capex of $105B, which only makes sense with continued growth. Offsets: N2 (3-4pt) and overseas-fab (2-4pt) GM dilution and rising depreciation, so growth decelerates from ~30% (2027 consensus) to ~18%.

Stock is at 20.9x FY2027 consensus today. I cut my round-1 20x by 0.5 turn because the 10-year hit ~5.24-5.29% (highest since 2002) and the Fed is hiking: a 19.5x multiple is a ~5.1% earnings yield, about level with the 10-year, which is as far as I would go for ~18% growth with GM dilution building. Not lower, because estimates are still rising 9/0 and TSMC is sole source at the leading edge.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FY27 FCF/ADR $12.55 (OCF 1.32x NI $113.7B less $85B capex); FCF growth 15/22/18/12%; cost of equity 10.0%; terminal growth 4%; net cash $18.6/ADR; valued at end-2027

inputs_detail.derivation: $21.93 consensus ADR EPS x 5.186B ADR-equivalents (25.93B common shares / 5)
2025 OCF NT$2,275B / net income NT$1,718B = 1.32. Q2 2026 OCF NT$783B vs net income ex-VIS gain ~NT$643B = 1.22 (tax-payment timing); rising D&A with capex supports holding ~1.3x for 2027.

Round 1 used $75B, which BofA describes as the market consensus. Sell-side updates since: GS $78B, BofA $85B, UBS $90B (Sep 28, via a Substack recap). The Aug board appropriation of $29.4B and the CFO's 'significantly higher' wording point to the upper half, so I use $85B: above consensus, a bit below the supervisor's $88B because UBS's figure is only available second-hand.

2028 is held to 15% because UBS has capex rising again to $105B; growth then picks up as capex intensity normalizes from ~37% of revenue and depreciation shields cash, then fades as the AI build-out matures (CEO: demand strong to 2029-30).

5.25% 10-year (Oct 1) + 4.0% equity risk premium at beta ~1 + 0.75pt for Taiwan geopolitics (Polymarket 13% invasion by end-2027) and 78% top-10 customer concentration. Round 1 used 9.5% on an ~8.5% equity cost that did not reflect a 5%+ risk-free rate.
June 30, 2026: cash NT$3,134B + marketable securities NT$820B - bonds NT$815B - LT bank loans NT$49B = NT$3,090B, /32 /5.186B ADRs. Round 1 had $15.4 from a rough debt guess.

bear.story: AI capex digestion in 2027 while TSMC spends $85-90B: orders from the top-2 customers slow, N2 and overseas-fab dilution push GM toward 58-60%, FY2028 EPS stalls near $22, and with a 5%+ 10-year the multiple compresses to ~13-14x. Includes a small tail for a Taiwan-strait shock or Section 232 tariffs.

base.story: 2026 closes at ~+40% USD revenue growth as guided, 2027 EPS lands near the $21.9 consensus on ~$229B revenue with 3-6% wafer price increases largely already in estimates, and the market pays ~19-19.5x for ~$24.9 NTM EPS in Oct 2027 as rates stay high.

bull.story: AI demand keeps beating, price increases stick, N2 dilution fades faster, FY2028 EPS reaches ~$28, and rates ease off their 2002-type highs, letting the multiple go to ~23x.

thesis_break_reason: $330 is ~15x the $21.93 FY2027 consensus, a trough-cycle multiple, ~28% below spot. Getting there would most likely require 2027 estimates to be cut (AI order pushouts from the top-2 customers, 36% of 2025 revenue, or a GM reset below ~58%) or a geopolitical/tariff repricing. High rates alone account for perhaps 1-1.5 turns of multiple (~$25-35), not $130, so I keep $330 rather than raising it.

key_uncertainties: How long AI accelerator demand lasts into 2027-28: TSMC's top two customers were 36% of 2025 revenue
Gross margin path: 3-4pt N2 dilution plus 2-4pt overseas-fab dilution against pricing power
Capex intensity: sell side now at $75-90B for 2027 (GS $78B, BofA $85B, UBS $90B) and UBS $105B for 2028, which holds FCF to ~$12-13/ADR
Rates: 10-year at ~5.25% (highest since 2002) and a hiking Fed cap the exit multiple
Geopolitics: Polymarket prices 13% for a China invasion of Taiwan by end-2027; tariffs/Section 232
Quality of reported EPS: Q2 2026 non-operating income of ~NT$96B, of which NT$63.2B was the VIS disposal/revaluation gain; a 2026 one-off that is not in FY27/FY28 estimates
TWD/USD moves: guidance assumes NT$32; spot 31.93
reasoning: Round 2 keeps the primary-document picture from round 1 and corrects three inputs flagged by the supervisor, after checking each. (1) Capex: my $75B for 2027 was the market consensus (BofA), but GS ($78B), BofA ($85B) and UBS ($90B, Sep 28) have moved up. I use $85B, which cuts FY27 FCF/ADR from $14.5 to $12.55. (2) Rates: the 10-year hit its highest since 2002 on Oct 1 (~5.24%, CNBC/Bloomberg) and the Fed hiked on Sep 16. I rebuilt the cost of equity as 5.25% + 4.0% ERP + 0.75pt Taiwan/concentration = 10.0% (was 9.5%) and trimmed the exit P/E from 20x to 19.5x. (3) Event date: September revenue is Oct 8 (TSMC calendar). I also replaced my net-cash guess with the 2Q26 consolidated balance sheet: NT$3.09T, or $18.6/ADR. The supervisor's VIS finding (NT$63.2B gain in Q2) confirms my round-1 EPS-quality flag, and it does not touch FY27 consensus ($21.93, revised 9 up / 0 down). Valuation: P/E leg 19.5 x $24.9 = $486; DCF $353 (15/22/18/12% FCF growth, 4% terminal). I moved the weights from 0.6/0.4 to 0.7/0.3 because the market prices TSMC on earnings and a 5-year DCF with a 4% terminal is structurally low for an 18%-growth franchise in a capex peak. That blends to ~$446, 3% below spot, down from $469; the supervisor suggested ~$445-455 and I land at the bottom of that range. The ladder is driven more by where a P/E-priced stock will trade in Oct 2027 than by the DCF: I put the median at ~$482 (19.5x x $24.9 minus a little for the rate-driven left skew), down from ~$497, with lognormal sigma 0.31 (40% realized vol shaded for mega-cap mean reversion) and a 5% crash component (median ~$210) for Taiwan/tariff shocks. The supervisor reviewed the crash weight and left it unchanged; it stays lighter than Polymarket's 13% because that market runs 3 months past the horizon and an invasion is not the same as an equity wipeout. Result: P(>=459) = 0.536, P(>=505) = 0.42, P(>=689) = 0.118. The upper tail is thinner than round 1 because of rates. Scenarios: 22% bear $290 / 56% base $480 / 22% bull $650 (mean ~$476). Where I differ from the supervisor: capex at $85B rather than $88B, because the UBS $90B is only available through a Substack recap and consensus is still ~$75B; and the thesis break stays at $330, because rates explain only ~1 turn of multiple. Research limits: the 2Q26 cash-flow statement and D&A were not in the 6-K excerpt I could fetch, so OCF/NI rests on 2025 and the CFO's Q2 call remarks.
